**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve explicitly initialized zero budgets**

When the colliding budget was deliberately initialized with `budgeted_spending = 0` (and possibly zero expected income), every `nonzero?` check here is false even though `Budget#initialized?` treats any non-nil spending value as an initialized plan. The importer therefore overwrites that user's existing plan with the exported values; before this change the uniqueness validation preserved it by rejecting the import. Restrict reuse to a genuinely uninitialized budget rather than treating an explicit zero plan as untouched.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Account for reused budgets in readback verification**

When this new branch handles the intended fresh-family collision, the budget count does not increase, and any preexisting zero category rows updated by `import_budget_categories` do not increase the budget-category count either. `SureImport#build_readback_verification` still expects every `Budget` and `BudgetCategory` line to create a row, while `SureImport#reused_counts_from` discounts only category/tag/merchant updates, so a successful restore records `readback_verification.status == "mismatch"` (for example, one expected budget versus zero actual). Include the newly reused budget and budget-category updates in readback accounting so API consumers do not receive a false integrity mismatch.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**Exclude initialized budgets from reuse.** A saved `budgeted_spending` value of `0` makes `Budget#initialized?` return true. `BudgetsController#update` permits saving that value, but `untouched_household_budget` rejects only nonzero values. The importer can therefore reuse the budget and overwrite both its parent values and category allocations. The untouched default remains reusable because `Budget.find_or_bootstrap` leaves the parent `budgeted_spending` nil. The zero values are assigned only to seeded `BudgetCategory` rows.
🐛 Suggested fix
```diff --- "a/app/models/family/data_importer.rb" +++ "b/app/models/family/data_importer.rb" @@ -1343,10 +1343,11 @@ # alone, so the import fails on the uniqueness validation rather than overwriting it. An exported # personal budget (with a user) is never merged into the household budget. def untouched_household_budget(start_date, end_date) budget = @family.budgets.find_by(user_id: nil, start_date: start_date, end_date: end_date) return if budget.blank? + return if budget.initialized? return if budget.budgeted_spending.to_d.nonzero? || budget.expected_income.to_d.nonzero? return if budget.budget_categories.any? { |budget_category| budget_category.budgeted_spending.to_d.nonzero? } budget end ```

Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements. ```suggestion return if budget.initialized? return if budget.budgeted_spending.to_d.nonzero? || budget.expected_income.to_d.nonzero? ```

After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. Visit https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli?utm_source=ghpr ```

`nonzero?` conflates "default/never touched" with "explicitly set to 0" for `budgeted_spending`/`expected_income`, which is a different (and weaker) definition than the one the model already uses: `Budget#initialized?` is `budgeted_spending.present?`, i.e. non-nil.

These fields have no DB default and start out `nil`; a user who deliberately zeroes out the household budget (e.g. types `0` into the budget-amount field, which the controller permits directly) ends up with `budgeted_spending = 0`, not `nil`. With this check, that budget is indistinguishable from a freshly-bootstrapped, never-touched one and will be silently reused and overwritten by the imported values — discarding the user's explicit choice.

Suggest matching the existing semantics instead, e.g. `return if budget.initialized? || budget.expected_income.present?`, so only a budget whose top-level fields are still `nil` is considered untouched. (Per-category `budgeted_spending` is non-nullable and defaults to `0` on bootstrap, so the `nonzero?` check there doesn't have this same nil/zero ambiguity — though it has the same inherent limitation that an explicit "plan to spend $0" on a category can't be distinguished from "never touched".)

**Reject duplicate `BudgetCategory` pairs in preflight.** A normal export from this repository cannot contain duplicate `(budget_id, category_id)` pairs because the exporter emits persisted rows and the database has a unique index. A hand-edited NDJSON file can contain them because preflight validates references and duplicate source IDs, but not duplicate `BudgetCategory` pairs. When repeated rows map to the same target, `find_or_initialize_by` overwrites the earlier `budgeted_spending` value. The new reuse accounting then checks only row-count deltas, so readback can report `matched` while the earlier allocation is lost. Reject duplicate pairs in preflight, or make this case produce a readback mismatch.

Thanks, that is a fair catch: `nonzero?` treated a budget the user deliberately set to 0 as untouched. Pushed a follow-up commit that uses the model's own definition as suggested: the default budget is reused only when `!budget.initialized? && budget.expected_income.blank?`, so any non-nil top-level amount (an explicit 0 included) keeps the import failing on the uniqueness validation instead of overwriting the plan. The per-category `nonzero?` check is unchanged, with the inherent limitation you describe.

Added a test with a budget set to `budgeted_spending: 0, expected_income: 0` that expects `RecordInvalid` and an untouched 0; it fails on the previous commit and passes now.

Second change in the same push (CodeRabbit/Codex readback point): when the default budget is reused, `Budget`/`BudgetCategory` rows are reported as `updated`, not created, so `SureImport#reused_counts_from` now discounts `budgets` and `budget_categories` as it already does for categories, tags and merchants. Without it the readback verification reported `mismatch` (expected 1 budget, actual 0) on a correct import. New test in `sure_import_test.rb` imports over an untouched default budget and expects `matched`; it fails without the change.

Disclosure: this change was prepared with an AI coding agent (Claude).
